3.title: Make partner operations durably idempotent
3.summary: Adds database-backed replay for the five operations accepted by `POST /api/v1/partner-batches`. The first stored submission for an `operation_id` determines its result; equivalent retries reuse that result, changed payloads conflict, and handled rejections retain their original details. Adds an `operations` audit table and `GET /api/v1/operations/:operation_id`. Reservation economics are unchanged; existing validation tests are adjusted to use distinct identifiers for distinct attempts.

changes.title: Replay operations by `operation_id` and complete JSON payload
changes.required: Use `operation_id` to prevent duplicate effects. An equivalent retry must return its stored result. Ignore JSON object key order; preserve array order and values. A different payload under an existing identifier must return `operation_id_conflict` without replacing the record.
changes.before: `GroupStay.Partner.process_operation/1` passed each submission into `run/1` and domain validation, even when its `operation_id` had already appeared. For example, a repeated payment could apply again if its amount and revision remained valid.
changes.after: `process_identified/2` looks up the operation before dispatching it. Existing records go to `replay/3`, which returns `record.result` when canonical JSON matches or `operation_id_conflict` otherwise. Only an unused identifier reaches the existing five operation handlers. Canonicalization sorts object keys recursively and retains array order.

verification.text: Source and assertions for repeated payments, batch retries, object and array order, changed amounts, and changed JSON types were inspected. The earlier independent review reran the 154-test candidate suite successfully. No additional concurrent-request test was run.

changes.title: Preserve rejected results and original revision details
changes.required: Remember handled rejections as well as applied results. Exact retries must preserve the original revision or stale-revision details even after domain state changes. Correcting `expected_revision` under the same `operation_id` is a conflicting payload.
changes.before: A repeated operation read the group again and checked its current revision. The existing credit test submitted the same identifier and payload twice and expected an applied result followed by `stale_revision`.
changes.after: Applied and rejected results are stored and returned directly on equivalent retries. A stored `group_not_found` remains that rejection after the group is created; a stored `actual_revision` is not refreshed. The credit revision test now gives its second attempt a new identifier so it still tests a fresh stale-revision rejection.

verification.text: The stored-result path and tests for remembered rejections, applied revisions, stale revisions, and corrected-revision conflicts were inspected. The earlier independent review reran the 154-test candidate suite successfully. The changed credit revision test was compared with M2.

changes.title: Commit operation records with successful changes and preserve failure behavior
changes.required: Commit successful domain changes and their operation record in one database transaction. Concurrent retries must have at-most-once effects. Handled rejections must leave domain state unchanged, commit their result, and allow later batch operations to run. Unexpected exceptions must roll back the current operation, remain unrecorded, and abort the HTTP request with `500`.
changes.before: `run/1` wrapped domain dispatch in a transaction. A handled rejection rolled back that transaction, and `process_batch/1` continued with the next operation. There was no durable operation record to commit or unique identifier constraint to arbitrate retries.
changes.after: A successful dispatch inserts its result before the transaction commits. An insertion error rolls back that attempt and rechecks the stored identifier. A handled rejection rolls back the domain transaction, then inserts its rejection record separately. Unexpected exceptions are not converted into remembered rejections. Operations without a usable identifier return `invalid_operation` without reaching the domain or operation table.

verification.text: Transaction boundaries and uniqueness handling were inspected. The candidate fault test asserts HTTP 500, rollback of the faulting operation, no stored result, and no following payment. The earlier independent review reran the 154-test suite successfully. No additional concurrency or crash-interruption experiment was run.

changes.required: Retain each remembered operation’s type, complete submitted content, exact result, and first-commit order. Records must survive application and database-process restarts. Earlier operations need no reconstruction because the gateway starts a new identifier namespace at deployment.
changes.before: The schema stored groups, rooms, credit lots, and credit redemptions. The batch handler returned operation results without storing complete submissions or results in an operation table.
changes.after: The migration adds `operations` with a unique `operation_id`, optional `type`, canonical `request_payload`, map-valued `result`, timestamps, and the generated primary key. `remember/3` inserts a record, `submitted_content/1` decodes its payload, and `in_commit_order/0` orders records by primary key. The migration creates an empty table and does not backfill earlier submissions.

4.title: Add room accounting and payment reductions
4.summary: Add room-level funding allocations, selected-room cancellation, cash-payment reductions, chargebacks with credit clawback, and a payment-reconciliation endpoint. Migrate existing group funding into allocations while preserving durable operation results.

changes.title: Expose room accounting in group responses
changes.required: Add `rooms[].status`, `rooms[].deposit_due_cents`, `rooms[].cash_paid_cents`, and `rooms[].credit_paid_cents` to group responses. Group lodging, due, paid, and outstanding totals must sum active rooms only.
changes.before: Room responses contain only `room_id` and `nightly_rate_cents`. Group responses expose aggregate lodging/deposit/funding amounts; cancellation retains historical amounts.
changes.after: Room responses add the four required fields. Group totals are recomputed from active rooms while the group remains active. When it becomes cancelled, stored totals freeze; the attached cancellation finding documents that exception.

verification.text: Source and cited candidate tests inspected. The complete candidate suite passed 233 tests in an isolated copy; no fresh targeted reproduction was added for this change unit.

changes.title: Cancel selected rooms and settle their funding
changes.required: `cancel_rooms` accepts distinct active `room_ids`, applies existing cancellation rules to their allocations, and returns IDs in original room order. Calculate the credit bonus once over combined selected cash. `cancel_group` settles remaining active rooms. With none left, status is cancelled and active-room group totals must be zero.
changes.before: Only `cancel_group` exists; it settles aggregate group cash/credit. Its group response preserves historical totals.
changes.after: Both operations use room-level settlement. Invalid selections return `invalid_rooms`; selected rooms become cancelled and receive settlement accounting. Partial cancellation recomputes remaining totals. Final cancellation instead freezes previous totals: this is a reproduced requirement mismatch.

verification.text: P2 finding reproduced in isolated `reviewer_active_totals_test.exs`: open two rooms, pay 10,000 cents, cancel room A, then room B. Zero active rooms remain; group lodging=52,500, due=10,500, paid=1,000 cents; required active totals=0. Ledger held=0 and refunded=10,000. Original candidate suite: 233 passed. Reviewer test: 0/1 passed, exit 2. Source tests preserve old full-cancellation totals or omit final due/paid assertions. Full-cancellation path inspected, not separately reproduced.
